claims.claim: Bounded Fibonacci address streams and Cassini-certified journal entries reject forgery and regression.
Block files are atomically flushed before the journal commit; replay checks sequence, schema, address, block size and SHA-256 before exposing payloads.
A backup, restore and explicit truncate-to-verified-prefix path is available; recovery preserves a journal backup.
Payloads, address indices, journal entries, queue slots and files are bounded and symlinked storage entries are rejected.
The declared bounded payload encoding round-trips without truncation.
Python and native queue writers/readers coordinate with an advisory process lock; readers reject unstable sequence records.
Manifold repair candidates must match an ingest-time digest; unrecoverable corruption returns no payload.
Pathfinder fallback is configurable, records a bounded reason and delegates exactly to the existing bisection query; output equivalence between engines is not claimed.
CPU fallback is policy-gated and explicit GPU requirements reject unavailable, unsupported or non-GPU execution.
OpenCL device execution, Chronus integration and CPU/OpenCL parity on deployed hardware.
A configurable harness supports up to one million writes; full-scale runtime, resource and recovery behavior have not been run here.
The root project includes Aethel sources, py.typed and documentation; isolated wheel/sdist install validation remains a deployment gate.
The deployment image and target container have not been built and exercised as part of this software audit.
SHA-256 detects accidental or unauthorized payload changes relative to the local journal but is not a keyed authenticity mechanism.
Aethel makes no quantum-speedup or unlimited-storage claim.
